title: Fear not, there is a way
hook: a student runs to a teacher, saying the world is on fire; the teacher's first words are: don't be afraid
carry: fear not: bondage is a misunderstanding

segments.voice: Yesterday: the boy and the crocodile, and Advaita's three rare things: a human birth, the longing for freedom, and a great soul's company. Today, what that great soul says first.

Two in the morning, and the phone lights up. A friend whose week has fallen apart all at once: work, money, a parent in the hospital. It isn't the moment for a lecture, or even a plan. Not yet. So what do you say first? The Vivekachudamani has a scene like this. A student arrives saying his whole world is on fire, and a teacher has to choose, carefully, his first words.
screen: `TWO IN THE MORNING.` → `A FRIEND'S WEEK ON FIRE.` → `WHAT DO YOU SAY FIRST?`

segments.voice: First, the book describes the teacher. Learned, yes, and more: free of desire. Calm, like a fire that has burned through its fuel. And kind without a reason: an ocean of mercy that doesn't need you to earn it. Then the student comes, bows, and pours it out. Paraphrased: master, friend of those who bow to you, I've fallen into the ocean of birth and death. I'm burning in a forest fire that has no end. Save me. The teacher looks at him with compassion and says, paraphrased: don't be afraid, wise one. There is no danger for you. There is a way across this ocean. Before any teaching, before any not two: don't be afraid. There's a way. Then the student asks his questions, and they're the whole book's table of contents. What is bondage? How did it come? How does it stay? How do I get free? What is not the self? And what is the self? The teacher's first move, after the comfort, is praise. You've asked well, he says. This is the Hindu way with a guru: you come humbly, with questions, and on the jnana path questions aren't a sign you're failing. They're the way in. And his answer to what is bondage is pure Advaita: bondage is taking what isn't the self to be the self. The rope, taken for a snake. The whole fire is burning on a misunderstanding. That's why the teacher can say, calmly: don't be afraid. And today? The doubts you're scared to say out loud are, on this path, exactly where it starts.
screen: `CALM, KIND WITHOUT A REASON.` · `I'M BURNING. SAVE ME.` · `DON'T BE AFRAID. THERE IS A WAY.` · `YOU'VE ASKED WELL.` · then, large: `BONDAGE IS A MISUNDERSTANDING.`

segments.voice: Name, gently, whatever is burning for you lately, and imagine someone completely calm, kind for no reason, sitting across from you and saying: don't be afraid, there is a way. Breathe in with that, and let the shoulders drop a little as you breathe out; you don't need the way yet, just the first sentence. If you pray, you can hear it as coming from God, or from a teacher you trust.
Advaita, in the Vivekachudamani's first scene: the student burning, the teacher calm. Don't be afraid, there is a way. Bondage is taking the not-self for the self.
Your line: fear not. Bondage is a misunderstanding, and there is a way. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Advaita tradition the teacher-student relationship is central: students approach a teacher with humility and questions, and the Vivekachudamani's opening dialogue is often read as the model for how that meeting should go.

Verse numbers vary by edition; the scene falls roughly in vv. 33–50. 'Fear not, wise one' (ma bhaishta vidvan) recalled as v. 43; confirm.
The six questions (bondage, its origin, its persistence, release, not-self, supreme self) paraphrased; confirm.
The answer to 'what is bondage' is summarized from later in the text.
